transcript: Yesterday I went to the West Village to see night of the Burning Pestle, a co production between Red Bull Theater and fiasco. This is an old play first performed in the 16 hundreds and in it we see a troop of actors about to put on a play called The London Merchant. They're interrupted by a pair of audience members who aren't interested in seeing just another story of love, chivalry and royalty and who instead demand a story that represents them and that features their apprentice who is with them at the theater. The players then improvise a version of the London Merchant to incorporate the apprentice who plays a grocer, and much of the show is a satire on high brow romantic dramadies and a satire on audiences. Although the dialogue is in Old English, the production felt modern in its themes and comedic sensibility and I thought it was a really fun Celebration of theatre as reflection and s community. With that, another program for my collection.
